correctness.rationale: Finite Weyl-conjugacy Fourier transform identifies lifting rank with the nonzero ambiguity support. For p prime and gcd(p,m)=1, Q(ζ_m) is linearly disjoint from Q(ζ_p), making Φ_p irreducible; any nonempty proper overlap at nonzero modulation gives a coefficient polynomial with at least one zero coefficient and cannot be scalar Φ_p, so no such ambiguity vanishes. At modulation zero, for each u the edges t→t+u within proper S are disjoint paths rather than cycles; freely chosen μ_m edge labels integrate to a valid vertex mask g. Lam–Leung vanishing-sum weights give exactly the nonnegative semigroup generated by prime divisors of m, yielding necessity AND sufficiency of the all-alphabet condition. The p=31 QR set has λ(u)=7 for u≠0; direct exact 6th-root checks of the stated phase assignment found precisely zero shifts ±1 and rank 959, while 7∉2N and 7∉3N. The explicit certificate and finite support checks corroborate but do not replace the all-prime proof.

value.rationale: Universal robustness of structured Gabor matrix tomography under a finite phase alphabet is a natural code-design property. The overlap-length semigroup gives a complete, efficiently checked classification rather than an isolated computation, and the 31-cycle example shows a genuinely composite-alphabet obstruction invisible to binary or ternary checks alone.

limitations: Only proper nonempty support on prime cyclic group, p≥5, gcd(p,m)=1; no extension to p|m or full support.
Matrix-level rank does not directly decide all pure-signal phase-retrieval fibers.
